title: Circles, solids and coordinate figures
lines: Circle and solid questions are formula questions with a twist: the formula is easy, but you must spot which length you are given (radius or diameter, slant side or height) and how the pieces of a figure fit together. Answers usually stay in terms of π.
## Circle basics
- Radius r, diameter d = 2r. Circumference C = 2πr = πd. Area A = πr².
- All radii of one circle are equal, so any triangle with two radii as sides is isosceles.
> A circle has circumference 10π. Find its area.
> 2πr = 10π, so r = 5 and A = 25π (about 78.5).
! Read whether the question gives the radius or the diameter. A diameter of 10 means an area of 25π, not 100π.
## Arcs and sectors
- A central angle of x° cuts off the fraction x/360 of the circle.
- Arc length = (x/360) × 2πr. Sector area = (x/360) × πr².
> In a circle of radius 10, a central angle is 72°. Find the arc length and the sector area.
> Arc length = (1/5)(20π) = 4π. Sector area = (1/5)(100π) = 20π.
! Arc length is a length (units), sector area is an area (square units). Answer choices often offer both.
## Chords
- A chord joins two points of the circle; the longest chord is a diameter.
- The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord. This makes a right triangle with the radius as hypotenuse.
> A chord of length 16 lies in a circle of radius 10. How far is it from the centre?
> Half the chord is 8. Distance = √(10² − 8²) = √36 = 6.
## Tangents
- A tangent touches the circle at one point and is perpendicular to the radius at that point.
- The two tangent segments from one outside point are equal in length.
> Point P is 13 units from the centre of a circle of radius 5. Find the length of a tangent from P.
> The radius meets the tangent at 90°, so tangent = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12.
## Inscribed angles
- An inscribed angle (vertex on the circle) is half the central angle that cuts off the same arc.
- An angle inscribed in a semicircle is 90°: if a triangle in a circle has a diameter as one side, it is a right triangle. The reverse also holds.
- Inscribed angles that cut off the same arc are equal.
> A central angle cuts off an arc and measures 110°. An inscribed angle cuts off the same arc. Find it.
> A right triangle with legs 6 and 8 is inscribed in a circle. Find the circle's area.
> The hypotenuse is a diameter: √(36 + 64) = 10, so r = 5 and the area is 25π.
## Composite figures
- Split the figure into pieces you know, then add, or take a big shape and subtract the unshaded part.
- Shaded region = outer area − inner area is the most common setup.
> A circle is inscribed in a square of side 10. Find the area inside the square but outside the circle.
> The circle's diameter is 10, so r = 5.
> A running track is a 100 m by 60 m rectangle with a semicircle on each short side. Find its perimeter (the outer edge).
> Two straight sides of 100 m: 200 m. The two semicircles make one full circle of diameter 60: 60π ≈ 188.5 m.
> Perimeter = 200 + 60π ≈ 388.5 m. The short sides of the rectangle are inside the figure, so they are not counted.
## Rectangular solids and cubes
- Volume = lwh. Surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh). The longest diagonal = √(l² + w² + h²).
- Cube of side s: V = s³, surface area 6s², diagonal s√3.
> A box measures 3 × 4 × 12. Find its volume, surface area and longest diagonal.
> A cube has volume 64. Find its surface area.
## Cylinders
- Volume = πr²h. Curved (lateral) surface = 2πrh. Total surface = 2πrh + 2πr².
- Doubling the radius multiplies the volume by 4; doubling the height doubles it.
> A cylinder has radius 3 and height 10. Find its volume and total surface area.
> Lateral = 2π(3)(10) = 60π; the two circles add 2π(9) = 18π; total = 78π.
> Water fills a 20 × 10 × 9 cm box to the brim and is poured into a cylinder of radius 5 cm. How high does it rise?
> Water volume = 1,800 cm³. Height = 1,800/(25π) = 72/π ≈ 22.9 cm.
! If a cylinder is open at the top (a can without a lid), only one circle counts in the surface area.
## Figures on the coordinate plane
- Use horizontal and vertical distances as base and height when a side lies along a grid line.
- Distance formula and midpoint formula from the functions lesson apply to any side.
- A circle with centre (h, k) and radius r has equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r².
> Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (6, 0) and (2, 5).
> The base on the x-axis is 6; the height is the y-coordinate of the third vertex, 5.
> Is (5, 3) on the circle (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25?
! In (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25 the centre is (2, −1): the signs inside are opposite to the coordinates.
## QC and timing advice
- If a figure is not drawn to scale, a point that looks like the centre may not be. Only a stated centre, diameter or tangent counts.
- Compare π answers without the calculator: π ≈ 3.14, so 25π ≈ 78.5 and 8π ≈ 25.
- Keep answers in π until the end; most choices are written that way. Convert with the calculator only for decimal choices.
> Quantity A: the area of a circle with circumference 12. Quantity B: 12.
> r = 12/(2π) = 6/π, so the area is π(36/π²) = 36/π ≈ 11.46. Quantity B is greater.
